CIV.note: Training is for youth, students and entrepreneurs, not civil servants.
Skills centres, not a programme bringing internet access to rural areas; no rural-urban use split.

facts.fact: GGGI says it launched the USD 8.25 million GENIE project with KOICA in partnership with the Government of Côte d'Ivoire on 26 February 2025, to set up 35 centres training over 45,000 people in digital literacy and ICT skills, with centres still being set up and about ten to open by mid-2025.

systems.owner: GGGI, KOICA, Government of Côte d'Ivoire

CIV.note: Names SNDI as an implementing partner of a training project; no in-house capacity or system build stated.
No school internet or curriculum stated.
A donor project hopes for startups; no startup law, labelling or public fund stated.

facts.fact: GGGI says the GENIE project is establishing 35 centres as hubs for learning and innovation in Abidjan, San Pedro, Korhogo, Man, Daloa, Yamoussoukro and Bondoukou, with a green incubator planned by mid-2025 and all centres to open by end 2025.
